# DualSenseT — Pre-Publish Checklist & Setup Guide

Everything the agent generated + what you need to do manually.
Follow in order — takes about 30–60 minutes total.

---

## STEP 1: Add all generated files to your repo

Copy each file below into your local clone of DualsenseT, then commit and push.

```
LICENSE                                ← root of repo
README.md                              ← replace your existing one
CONTRIBUTING.md                        ← root of repo
CHANGELOG.md                           ← root of repo
SECURITY.md                            ← root of repo
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md  ← create this folder path
.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md
.github/workflows/ci.yml              ← create this folder path
```

Commands:
```bash
cd your/local/DualsenseT
# paste all the files in
git add .
git commit -m "chore: add LICENSE, README polish, CONTRIBUTING, issue templates, CI"
git push
```

---

## STEP 2: Add screenshots to the README (MOST IMPORTANT)

The README has a placeholder:
  Assets/screenshot-dashboard.png

Take screenshots of:
1. The main Dashboard (any tab — Triggers or Live Map looks best)
2. The Menu Bar icon showing battery status
3. The 3D Sensor card rotating

Add them to your Assets/ folder and update the README image path.
A screen recording GIF of the Live Map or 3D sensor card would go viral.
Tools: macOS built-in Screenshot.app (Cmd+Shift+5) or Gifox for GIFs.

---

## STEP 3: Set up the GitHub repo settings (2 minutes)

Go to https://github.com/DegenerateUSER/DualsenseT → Settings (gear icon top right of repo page, NOT your account settings)

a) DESCRIPTION — click the gear next to "About" on the right sidebar:
   Description: "Free, native macOS utility for PS5 DualSense adaptive triggers, LED, sensors & UDP emulation"
   Website: (leave blank for now or add a future landing page)
   Topics: add these tags:
     macos swift dualsense ps5 gamecontroller adaptive-triggers hid iokit swiftui

b) FEATURES — in the same Settings → General:
   ✅ Check "Issues"
   ✅ Check "Discussions" (turn this ON — great for community Q&A)
   ✅ Check "Preserve this repository" (optional but nice)

---

## STEP 4: Create your first Release (v1.0.0)

This is what makes the project feel "real" and lets people download a .app without building.

Option A — If you can build a .dmg or .zip of DualSenseT.app:
  1. Build: ./build.sh
  2. Zip the .app: zip -r DualSenseT-v1.0.0.zip DualSenseT.app
  3. Go to GitHub → Releases → "Create a new release"
  4. Tag: v1.0.0
  5. Title: "DualSenseT v1.0.0 — Initial Release"
  6. Upload the .zip as a release asset
  7. Paste a description (copy from CHANGELOG.md)

Option B — If you can't build a distributable yet:
  Just create the release anyway with source code only.
  People who want to try it can build with ./build.sh

---

## STEP 5: Verify GitHub Actions CI runs

After pushing, go to:
  https://github.com/DegenerateUSER/DualsenseT/actions

You should see a "Build & Test" workflow triggered.
If it fails (e.g. build.sh needs chmod or dependencies), fix and push again.
If it passes, you'll get a green checkmark badge — add it to your README:

  [![CI](https://github.com/DegenerateUSER/DualsenseT/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/DegenerateUSER/DualsenseT/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

Add that line right below the other badges in README.md.

---

## STEP 6: Share it (do this last, after steps 1-5)

Post in these places in this order:

1. Reddit r/macgaming
   Title: "I built a free, open-source macOS alternative to DualSenseM for PS5 DualSense — adaptive triggers, LED, gyro, UDP server for CrossOver/Wine games"

2. Reddit r/PS5
   Title: "Free macOS app for DualSense adaptive triggers — native Swift, no paid software needed"

3. Reddit r/SteamDeck (CrossOver users)

4. Hacker News "Show HN"
   Title: "Show HN: DualSenseT – Free macOS utility for PS5 DualSense adaptive triggers"

5. CrossOver / Whisky Discord servers

## WHAT THE AGENT GENERATED (summary)

| File | What it does |
|------|-------------|
| LICENSE | MIT license — required for open source |
| README.md | Polished readme with badges, feature table, usage, collapsible engineering sections |
| CONTRIBUTING.md | Guide for bug reports, feature requests, PRs |
| CHANGELOG.md | Version history starting with v1.0.0 |
| SECURITY.md | Explains how to report vulnerabilities privately |
| .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md | Structured bug report form on GitHub Issues |
| .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature_request.md | Feature request form |
| .github/workflows/ci.yml | GitHub Actions: auto-builds + runs tests on every push/PR |

---

## ONE THING YOU MUST DO MANUALLY

Add a LICENSE. Without it, the project is technically "All Rights Reserved" by default
even if it says open-source in the README. The generated LICENSE file fixes this.

---

Good luck — you built something genuinely useful. Ship it.
